_about: Phase 2 of the Universal PCB AI Engine — voltage-drop / current-density REPORT (a read-only check, not a fix). Consumed by tools/power_integrity_pcb.py. For every POWER net it measures the routed copper (total length + bottleneck width from the .kicad_pcb tracks), infers the net's design current (same source as the ampacity tool: layout_config.json:ampacity.net_current_a + power_net_patterns + class_design_current_a), then computes R = rho*L/A, Vdrop = I*R and current density J = I/A, and flags a WARNING when the drop or density exceeds the thresholds here or the trace is narrower than the IPC-2152 recommended width. Pure physics + config — no per-circuit logic. enabled=false makes the tool a no-op.
_units: resistivity in ohm*metre; distances mm; current A; voltage V; density A/mm^2. 1 oz copper = copper_thickness_mm_per_oz.
_resistivity_note: Annealed copper at 20 C. Copper's tempco is ~0.393%/C, so a rail running hot (60-90 C) has ~15-30% higher resistance and drop. Bump this (e.g. 2.1e-8 for ~70 C) or pass temp_c to model a hot board.
_min_power_note: Nets whose inferred design current is below this are treated as signal nets and skipped — power integrity only matters for rails.
_via_note: Approx series resistance added per via on the net (plated 0.3 mm barrel ~ 0.5-1 mOhm). Set 0 to ignore via resistance.
_vdrop_note: WARN when Vdrop exceeds vdrop_warn_pct of the rail voltage (when the rail voltage is known from the net name / net_voltages arg) OR exceeds vdrop_warn_abs_v absolute. 3 percent is the common rail-integrity budget for a logic supply.
_density_note: Advisory ceiling. IPC-2152 external 1 oz at ~10-20 C rise sits around 50 A/mm^2; above ~55 the trace runs hot. Scales physically with copper weight because a wider cross-section lowers J.
_width_note: WARN when the net's bottleneck (narrowest) track is more than width_margin_pct below the IPC-2152 recommended width for its current (read from ipc_constraints.json:width_by_current.bands). This is the honest 'trace too thin for its current' check.
